headline: Energy and Software Lead a Split Session as Chip Stocks Take a Beating
body_html:
Thursday's session closed with a modest but uneven advance across our 544-stock universe: 295 names finished higher while 245 ended in the red, leaving the tape tilted toward cautious optimism rather than conviction. The clearest theme was a sharp rotation away from semiconductors — the group shed 3.15% as a sector, the worst showing of the day — and toward energy, which climbed 1.58% amid escalating Middle East tensions that rattled air-travel routes and accelerated Asia's push to stockpile crude. Software added 1.36% and consumer names rose 1.11%, suggesting investors were willing to pay for earnings visibility as geopolitical risk premiums rose elsewhere.

The session's standout mover was Vita Coco (COCO), which surged 10.52% to lead all gainers in the consumer-beverages space. CoStar Group (CSGP) was close behind at plus 8.01%, with GoDaddy (GDDY) and eXp World Holdings (AGNT) also posting meaningful gains of 6.20% and 5.94%, respectively. On the downside, MaxLinear (MXL) bore the brunt of semiconductor selling, dropping 12.72%, while argenx (ARGX) fell 11.83% and Coherent (COHR) slid 9.62%, pulling networking and optical hardware sharply lower alongside chip-design names Arm Holdings (ARM, -6.48%) and Vicor Corporation (VICR, -7.24%).

What stands out is the breadth of the semiconductor selloff relative to the rest of the market: six of the day's ten worst performers trace directly to chip design, power electronics, or optical networking. With Friday's session now approaching, traders will be watching whether that group stabilizes or whether the rotation out of high-multiple technology deepens into the weekend.

briefs.headline: Houthi Escalation Disrupts Gulf Air Routes, Lifts Energy Trade
briefs.body: A drone strike damaged an aircraft at Riyadh's airport Thursday, prompting Lufthansa and several Indian carriers to suspend flights to the Saudi capital. The incident pushed energy markets higher as traders weighed supply-chain risk, contributing to the sector's 1.58% gain on the session.

briefs.headline: Fresh Iran Sanctions Add a Layer of Geopolitical Uncertainty
briefs.body: Washington imposed new sanctions targeting Iran's so-called shadow fleet of oil tankers, tightening the financial vice on Tehran's crude exports. The move comes as Asian nations are already racing to stockpile oil and accelerate renewable capacity in response to broader regional hostilities, according to Reuters.

briefs.headline: Treasury Adviser Signals Yields Could Ease from Elevated Levels
briefs.body: A senior adviser to Treasury Secretary Bessent characterized current Treasury yields as exceptionally high but expressed confidence they could decline in the near term. The comments offered a degree of reassurance to rate-sensitive sectors, though the software and homebuilder groups — up 1.36% and 1.02% — appeared to price in some relief already.

briefs.headline: Starbucks Data Encourages, but Chipotle Takeover Report Roils Consumer Space
briefs.body: New operational figures suggested Starbucks' turnaround effort is gaining traction, a positive for the broader consumer discretionary complex that rose 1.11% Thursday. However, an unconfirmed report about a potential Chipotle acquisition weighed on that stock specifically, underscoring how headline risk can cut both ways within a single sector on the same day.

briefs.headline: Germany Lifts Growth Outlook, Offering a Macro Tailwind
briefs.body: The German government revised its economic growth forecasts upward for both 2026 and 2027, a constructive data point for globally exposed industrials and materials names. The industrial sector managed a slim 0.16% gain Thursday, though materials slipped 0.45%, indicating the foreign demand optimism has yet to fully filter through to commodity-linked equities.

briefs.headline: Desk Adds to Positions Ahead of Catalysts as Chip Rout Creates Openings
briefs.body: Commentary from investment desks Thursday pointed to selective dip-buying in hard-hit names, with some managers citing upcoming catalysts as justification for adding exposure before the market fully reprices. The semiconductor sector's 3.15% decline — the steepest of any group in Thursday's session — appeared to be generating tactical interest even as broader selling continued.
